title: Submerged oil droplets shifted from two size peaks to one
summary: In a lab experiment with a submerged silicone-oil jet, image measurements showed two peaks in the volume-weighted droplet-size distribution in transitional flow. At higher Reynolds numbers the distribution shifted toward one peak with smaller characteristic droplets.
organization: Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad; Lehigh University

source_review.scope: §§3.5.1 and 4–5; measured droplet distributions and separate physical-model comparisons

evidence.tested: The analysis used fluorescence images from the controlled oil–water analogue and a U-Net trained on 200 manually annotated images. The source compared measurements with a physical population model.
evidence.unknown: The result describes a lab fluid pair and the tested flow regimes. The proposed breakup interpretation is supported by the accompanying flow analysis rather than independently established for all fluids.
evidence.ai_role: A trained segmentation network separated visible droplets from image artifacts so their detected sizes could be used to measure the distributions.
